item.title: 2026 Distinguished Teaching Award recipients announced
item.description: Five professors and lecturers from across campus received this year's award, which recognizes exceptional teaching that has a lifelong impact on students. The post 2026 Distinguished Teaching Award recipients announced appeared first on Berkeley News.

item.title: Peak leadership: MBA students embark on Mount Everest Base Camp trek - Haas News | UC Berkeley Haas
item.description: Esa Tilija, MBA 26, a Nepali-American from Seattle, will lead the first-ever UC Berkeley Haas student trek to Mount Everest Base Camp.

item.title: Psychedelic film series at BAMPFA opens doors to other worlds - Berkeley News
item.description: BAMPFA’s Kate MacKay explains Psychedelia & Cinema, a mind-bending film series that redefines the cinematic trip as a powerful tool for liberation and self-discovery.

item.title: Berkeley Talks: How 17th-century moveable scenery shaped modern theater - Berkeley News
item.description: UC Berkeley Professor Julia Fawcett discusses how Restoration-era stagecraft and London’s post-fire rebuilding mirrored each other, together redefining performance and urban life.

item.title: Lightning bolts on Jupiter pack more than 100 times the power of Earth’s flashes - Berkeley News
item.description: Larger, more powerful storms on Jupiter produce stronger lightning than on Earth. New measurements could shed light on electrical phenomena associated with thunderstorms on our planet.

item.title: From Sproul Plaza to 924 Gilman: How the East Bay helped define punk’s radical legacy - Berkeley News
item.description: A new book by UC Berkeley and Cornell professors reclaims the punk movement’s diverse, countercultural roots.

item.title: UC Berkeley reaches major housing milestone for incoming new students - Berkeley News
item.description: Progress on multiple new housing projects means all first-year students will have the option to live on campus for two years — with another major development in the pipeline.

item.title: Harnessing real-world data to bring life-saving drugs to the public sooner
item.description: Public health researchers are collaborating with the FDA and industry to make drug clinical trials faster and better.

item.title: From designated hitters to robot umpires, how baseball has — and hasn’t — changed over its 200-year history - Berkeley News
item.description: Before baseball’s opening day, UC Berkeley professor David Henkin talks about his new book, the origin of statistics mania and whether the sport has ever truly been “uniquely American.”
